 Wall Street ended the trading week higher, despite persistent concerns over inflation and the interest-rate outlook, as investors also digested the news of Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s chief executive officer.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares remained under pressure all week after the company announced that Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has resigned effective immediately.

 U.S. inflation remained stubbornly elevated in October, with CPI rising 0.4% month over month, exceeding economists’ expectations of a 0.3% increase.

 The hotter-than-expected inflation data puts a 50-basis-point rate hike back in consideration for December, while a 25-basis-point increase now appears largely priced in.

For the week, the blue-chip Dow ( DJI ) added +2%, the benchmark S&P ( SP500 ) popped +2.5%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) climbed +2.2%. Read a preview of next week's major events in Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Price gap 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha
 
 
Europe and Asia have borne the brunt of the Iran war-driven surge in natural gas prices, while the U.S. has largely been shielded from it. U.S. buyers pay around $3 per MMBtu for natural gas. But European and Asian consumers are currently paying a little over $30 per MMBtu. What's behind this wide price gap? Read more.
